company_name: Sany Heavy Equipment International Holdings Company Limited
overview: Sany International is a Cayman Islands-incorporated, HKEX-listed (since 2009) manufacturer of heavy equipment, part of the Sany Group ecosystem alongside its larger A-share/H-share affiliate Sany Heavy Industry/Sany Heavy Equipment (600031.SH/06031.HK). Its four segments are mining equipment (coal mining machinery, mining trucks, smart/unmanned mining systems), logistics equipment (port machinery such as gantry cranes, front loaders, stacking machines, forklifts), oil and gas equipment (frac spreads, drilling/workover, LNG EPC), and emerging industries (solar modules, hydrogen, lithium/power battery and energy storage systems, the last added via a July 2024 acquisition). The company is based in Shenyang/Hunan, PRC, and reports in RMB, with growing export sales to Asia, Africa, the Middle East and the Americas alongside its core China market.

business_model.summary: Sany International manufactures and sells capital equipment to mining, port/logistics and oil & gas operators, largely on a project/order basis rather than subscription revenue, supplemented by spare parts, services and financing-guarantee support for customer purchases. Growth has shifted from domestic coal mining machinery (structurally declining) toward mining trucks/unmanned vehicles, large port machinery, and the newly acquired lithium/energy-storage business, with overseas sales now the fastest-growing component (international revenue +13.0% in FY2025 to RMB9.23bn, 38% of revenue; +69.5% YoY in H1 2026 to RMB6.81bn).

revenue_streams.name: Mining equipment (coal machinery, mining trucks, smart mines)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed - domestic coal machinery declining, mining trucks growing fast (H1 2026 truck revenue +97.5% YoY)

revenue_streams.name: Logistics/port equipment (large & small port machinery, forklifts)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (large port machinery H1 2026 revenue +62.6% YoY)

revenue_streams.name: Oil and gas equipment (frac spreads, drilling, LNG EPC)
Emerging industries (solar, hydrogen, power battery/lithium, energy storage)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - lithium business acquired Jul-2024, power battery revenue +67.5% YoY in H1 2026

business_model.customer_type: B2B - mining operators, port authorities/terminal operators, oil & gas companies, utilities and industrial customers
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025 international revenue ~38% of total (RMB9.23bn of RMB24.33bn), growing faster than domestic; domestic China remains the largest single market but structurally challenged in coal machinery

main_competitors: Sany Heavy Industry/Sany Heavy Equipment (affiliate, A/H-share 600031.SH/06031.HK)
competitive_position.market_position: Leading domestic position in coal mining machinery (roadheaders, shearers) and a fast-growing challenger in mining trucks and port machinery; global port machinery market is concentrated among Liebherr, Konecranes, ZPMC, Cargotec and Sany, together holding the large majority of share, with ZPMC claiming the largest single share in ship-to-shore cranes/RTGs

moat_factors.factor: Sany Group brand and R&D scale
moat_factors.description: Benefits from the broader Sany Group's manufacturing scale, supply chain and brand recognition in construction/heavy machinery, and heavy continued R&D spend (~5.9% of FY2025 revenue) in electrification and unmanned/autonomous mining

moat_factors.factor: Cost advantage via domestic supply chain
moat_factors.description: Chinese manufacturing cost base supports competitive pricing versus Western incumbents (Komatsu, Caterpillar, Liebherr) in emerging markets

Claims to be first in China to offer integrated excavation, transport and smart-mine solutions; unmanned mining truck deployments (Hami, Xinjiang) show >90% equipment availability and >70% labor cost reduction versus peers in the same mining area
Large capital equipment creates some service/spare-parts stickiness but mining/port operators can and do multi-source from global OEMs

weaknesses: Sub-scale globally compared to Komatsu, Caterpillar, Liebherr and ZPMC in their respective core categories
Heavy reliance on a structurally shrinking domestic coal mining machinery market
New emerging-industries segment (solar, battery, hydrogen) is unproven at scale and entered a sector already suffering severe Chinese overcapacity/price wars
Lower overall gross margin (~22%) than Western equipment peers, with margin further pressured by growing mix of lower-margin products

growth_drivers: Mining truck business scaling rapidly (overtook coal mining machinery in FY2025 scale; H1 2026 truck revenue +97.5% YoY, overseas truck revenue +185.5% YoY) with a stated ambition to become a global leading mining equipment supplier by 2030
Unmanned/autonomous mining technology adoption, reducing customer labor costs >70% and improving output - a secular automation tailwind in mining

Globalization strategy - overseas sales growing far faster than domestic (FY2025 +13.0%, H1 2026 +69.5%), with APM Terminals global framework agreement for 500+ electric terminal tractors (largest such order globally) and expansion into Africa, MENA, Europe and Asia
Large port machinery and electrification of port equipment (electric reach stackers, terminal tractors, stacking machines) riding global port infrastructure upgrade demand
Lithium/energy storage business (acquired Jul-2024) diversifying into global energy transition, power battery revenue +67.5% YoY in H1 2026, first domestic hundred-MWh order secured Sep-2025
Management's explicit 2028 target: RMB57.5 billion in sales revenue (roughly 2.4x FY2025 revenue) and gross margin expansion to 24%

business.risk: Structural decline in domestic coal mining machinery demand
business.description: China's coal output growth is slowing to its lowest rate this decade amid overcapacity curbs and renewable substitution; the Group itself describes this market as 'under pressure with intense industry competition'

Lithium energy, solar, and hydrogen businesses are recent additions operating in highly competitive, overcapacity-plagued Chinese sectors; FY2024 goodwill impairment (~RMB470m, oil & gas) and a further RMB72m impairment in FY2025 highlight integration/valuation risk

Trade and bills receivables turnover days have been rising (199 to 201.5 days FY2025, still elevated at 190 days H1 2026) alongside growing financial guarantee contracts extended to customers' financing/leasing arrangements
Management explicitly flags 'intensifying competition and accelerating technological iteration' in H1 2026 commentary as a headwind to margins and share

financial.description: Gearing ratio rose from 63.2% (FY2024) to 63.9% (FY2025) to 67.1% (H1 2026); interest-bearing borrowings grew from RMB9.9bn to RMB11.3bn to fund emerging-industry capex

financial.risk: Working capital build and elongating payment terms
financial.description: Inventory and receivables days increased through FY2025 (inventory days 94→108.5), pressuring operating cash conversion even as H1 2026 showed some improvement

Growing overseas (USD/EUR-denominated) sales against an RMB reporting/functional currency base; ~RMB3.6bn of cash held in foreign currencies as a partial natural hedge, no formal hedging program disclosed

regulatory.description: Beijing has tightened mine safety/environmental inspections and capacity approvals, directly constraining the addressable market for coal mining machinery

regulatory.risk: Geopolitical/export restrictions on Chinese industrial exporters
regulatory.description: As a China-domiciled manufacturer increasingly reliant on exports (mining trucks, port machinery, energy equipment), the Group is exposed to tariff actions, trade restrictions, or politically motivated procurement barriers in Western and allied markets, similar to pressures faced by other Chinese heavy-equipment and EV-supply-chain exporters

macro.risk: China macro slowdown / industrial capex cycle
macro.description: Demand for mining, port and oil & gas equipment is tied to global commodity capex cycles and China's industrial activity, both cyclical

Steel, batteries/lithium and other industrial inputs affect manufacturing costs; management cites product mix shift toward lower-margin products as the main recent margin pressure rather than input costs specifically
Growing bank borrowings (RMB11.3bn as of H1 2026) at rates of ~1.3%-4.3% make finance costs sensitive to PRC and offshore rate movements; finance costs rose 17.5% YoY in H1 2026

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Domestic Chinese coal mining machinery demand is flat-to-declining amid overcapacity curbs and the energy transition, while global port infrastructure upgrades, mining electrification/automation, and energy storage adoption are structural growth areas the Group is pivoting toward
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - capital equipment orders for mining, oil & gas and port infrastructure are tied to commodity price cycles and global industrial/trade capex, with lumpy large-project revenue recognition
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - rising bank debt (~RMB11.3bn) funds capex and working capital; higher rates raise finance costs and customer financing costs, potentially slowing equipment orders
key_input_costs: Lithium/battery cell materials for the new energy storage business
Logistics/shipping costs for overseas equipment deliveries

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: revenue +20.5% YoY to RMB14.75bn, but profit attributable to owners fell 5.9% YoY to RMB1.22bn as gross margin compressed to 22.1% (from 23.7%) on product mix and higher finance/opex costs
Overseas revenue surged 69.5% YoY to RMB6.81bn in H1 2026 (46% of total revenue), led by mining trucks (+185.5% YoY overseas) and large port machinery (+82.3% YoY overseas)
Board leadership change: Mr. Liang Zaizhong resigned as Chairman (remains executive Director); Mr. Zhou Fugui, a long-time Sany Group/Sany Heavy Energy executive, appointed Chairman
Sany Lithium secured its first domestic hundred-MWh-level energy storage order, marking entry into large-scale energy storage projects

FY2025 results: revenue +11.1% to RMB24.33bn; profit attributable to owners +61.5% to RMB1.78bn, aided by a sharp reduction in impairment charges versus FY2024 (FY2024 included ~RMB470m oil & gas goodwill impairment and ~RMB278m impairment on properties held for sale, versus only RMB72m goodwill impairment in FY2025)
APM Terminals signed a Global Framework Agreement for Sany Marine Heavy Industry to supply 500+ electric terminal tractors - described as the world's largest such procurement
Delivered first 1-million-cubic-meter-scale natural gas liquefaction (LNG) EPC project (Guazhou Maoque), with 5 LNG projects completed and 6 new orders (>RMB900m) secured in the year
Completed acquisition of the lithium/power battery and energy storage business, adding a new revenue segment that has since grown rapidly (power battery revenue +67.5% YoY in H1 2026)

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026) / H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026)

items.notes: Implies roughly a 2.4x increase over FY2025 revenue of RMB24.3bn (~24% CAGR 2025-2028 if linear); stated in FY2025 annual report MD&A as a company-wide goal alongside gross margin target
Up from 22.3% in FY2025 and 22.1% in H1 2026 (margin has recently compressed, not expanded, making this target more aspirational)

items.target: Continue 'Globalisation, Digitalisation and Low-carbonisation' strategy; mining trucks/unmanned driving as 'strong growth drivers', port machinery as globalisation 'bridgehead', microgrids as mining-ecosystem 'adhesive'
items.notes: No specific quantitative KPI guidance beyond revenue/margin targets above; H1 2026 commentary added emphasis on 'planning transformation', meeting efficiency and company-wide AI adoption to improve organizational effectiveness

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Zhou Fugui's FY2025 statement framed underground mining equipment as the performance foundation, mining trucks/unmanned driving as the strongest growth driver, port machinery as the globalization bridgehead, and microgrids as the adhesive for the mining ecosystem, targeting global leadership in mining equipment by 2030. The H1 2026 statement struck a more cautious tone, citing a 'complex and volatile economic environment and intensifying competition' and emphasizing 'prudent operations' and 'lean operations' over aggressive growth, after H1 2026 profit fell YoY despite strong revenue growth.

bull_case: Mining truck and unmanned/autonomous mining technology businesses are scaling rapidly (truck revenue +97.5% YoY in H1 2026) and could become the company's largest and highest-growth segment, with productivity gains (>70% labor cost reduction) that are compelling for mine operators

Overseas expansion is outpacing China (H1 2026 overseas revenue +69.5% YoY, now 46% of total) diversifying away from the structurally declining domestic coal mining machinery market and capturing global port electrification/automation demand
Large anchor contracts (APM Terminals 500+ electric terminal tractor deal) signal credibility with top-tier global customers and a growing order book in large port machinery
New energy storage/lithium segment provides optionality on the global energy transition and has shown triple-digit growth in recent periods (power battery revenue +67.5% YoY)

Management has articulated a concrete, ambitious 2028 target (RMB57.5bn revenue, 24% gross margin) that, if credible, implies substantial upside from current ~RMB24bn revenue base; consensus analyst ratings are skewed toward Buy/Strong Buy with price targets above the recent trading range
bear_case: H1 2026 showed revenue growth decoupling from profit - profit attributable to owners fell 5.9% YoY even as revenue rose 20.5%, driven by gross margin compression and rising finance costs, raising doubt about the quality of growth and the achievability of the 2028 margin target

Domestic coal mining machinery, long the core franchise, faces structural headwinds from PRC overcapacity curbs, tightening environmental/safety regulation, and the broader energy transition reducing coal demand

Rising leverage (gearing ratio up from 63.2% to 67.1% in 18 months) and lengthening receivables/inventory days suggest growth is being funded by debt and working capital build rather than organic cash generation, with investing cash outflows also expanding sharply (H1 2026 investing outflow RMB2.03bn vs RMB92.6m inflow in H1 2025)

New emerging-industries bets (solar, hydrogen, lithium/battery) are entering sectors already suffering severe Chinese overcapacity and price competition, with a history of impairments (goodwill write-downs in FY2024 and FY2025) suggesting execution and valuation risk on M&A

As a Chinese industrial exporter increasingly reliant on international sales (46% of H1 2026 revenue), the company is exposed to geopolitical/trade-policy risk (tariffs, procurement restrictions) that could curtail its fastest-growing revenue stream
Mid-October 2025 chairman transition introduces leadership-continuity uncertainty at a time of strategic pivot toward new segments
